claims.text: Contrast ratio between two colors ranges from 1:1 (identical colors) to 21:1 (black on white); higher is easier to read.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs ui/accessibility/ui-design-and-styling.md (contrast); flutter_test accessibility.dart computeContrastRatio (WCAG formula)

claims.text: WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines) is a published standard with conformance levels such as AA and AAA; at level AA normal-size text needs a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, large text at least 3:1.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs ui/accessibility/ui-design-and-styling.md 'At least 4.5:1 for small text'; flutter_test accessibility.dart (WCAG AA/AAA levels)

claims.text: Large text in these rules is 18 point and above regular, or 14 point and above bold; smaller text counts as normal (small) text.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs ui/accessibility/ui-design-and-styling.md (contrast: 18 point regular / 14 point bold); flutter_test kLargeTextMinimumSize, kBoldTextMinimumSize

claims.text: flutter_test provides meetsGuideline with the guidelines textContrastGuideline (text contrast), androidTapTargetGuideline (tappable nodes at least 48x48) and labeledTapTargetGuideline (tap/long-press targets are labeled), run on what a widget test has built.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs ui/accessibility/accessibility-testing.md (Accessibility Guideline API example); Flutter API flutter_test: meetsGuideline, AccessibilityGuideline

claims.text: The guidelines read the semantics tree (screen reader description). testWidgets turns semantics on by default (semanticsEnabled: true); the test's tester.ensureSemantics() makes it explicit, as in Flutter's accessibility testing docs; dispose() releases that handle.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API testWidgets semanticsEnabled, WidgetTester.ensureSemantics, SemanticsHandle.dispose; Flutter docs accessibility-testing.md example

claims.text: textContrastGuideline compares each text found through semantics with the colors drawn behind it, against 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API flutter_test textContrastGuideline / MinimumTextContrastGuideline; accessibility-testing.md comment '3:1 for larger text (18 point and above regular)'

claims.text: meetsGuideline returns an AsyncMatcher (its check has to wait for a result), so it is used with await expectLater rather than expect.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API flutter_test meetsGuideline (AsyncMatcher); accessibility-testing.md example uses await expectLater

claims.text: At stage-3 components_accessibility_test.dart loops over galleryExamples (8 entries) and Brightness.values (light, dark), making 16 testWidgets named '<example> (<brightness>) meets the guidelines', each pumping exampleFrame and expecting the three guidelines.
exampleFrame builds the entry in MaterialApp with buildTheme(donHangBrand, brightness), in a 360 x 160 SizedBox on the theme's surface color; lib/main.dart uses buildTheme with the same donHangBrand.
At stage-3 ci.yml (on push except dependabot branches, pull_request) has an app job on ubuntu-24.04 running `flutter test` in DonHang.App; any failing test fails the job.

StatusBanner: info/error colors from colorScheme, warning/success from StatusColors (ThemeExtension, lib/design/status_colors.dart); values in lib/design/brand.dart, hand-written per theme; its comment says each 'on' color keeps at least 4.5:1, tested here.
In galleryExamples only message_view_action (Reload) and status_banner_action (Remove) have a tappable action.
ThemeData does not compare a ThemeExtension's colors with each other; nothing in the theme checks warning against onWarning.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API ThemeData.extensions, ThemeExtension (no validation); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 lib/design/theme.dart

claims.text: labeledTapTargetGuideline checks that a tap target has a label, not what the label says; a wrongly worded label passes.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API flutter_test labeledTapTargetGuideline; accessibility-testing.md 'Checks that touch targets with a tap or long press action are labeled'

claims.text: When accessibility depends on a whole flow (reading order, meaning of labels, finishing an order with a screen reader), automated per-widget guidelines are not enough and a person should try it.
Turning 'is it readable' into a measured contrast ratio lets a test check it identically on every run and machine, unlike judging by eye on one screen.

With dark onWarning set to 0xFF7A5900 on dark warning 0xFFF5C451 the contrast is about 4:1 (computed ~3.96:1), so the 14-sp bodyMedium banner text fails textContrastGuideline: only 'status_banner_warning (dark) meets the guidelines' of 16 fails.
claims.source_hint: WCAG relative luminance formula; run flutter test test/design/components_accessibility_test.dart at stage-3 with the edit; status_banner.dart:51 bodyMedium

claims.text: git switch --detach <tag> checks out the tag's commit without a branch; git restore <file> discards the working-tree change to that file.
